texts.preamble: Jai Narain vs State Of U.P. on 22 December, 2023 Author: Samit Gopal Bench: Samit Gopal High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:243022 Court No. - 69 Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 283 of 2013 Revisionist :- Jai Narain Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
texts.facts: The facts of the present case are that the then Food Inspector Dalveer Singh inspected the shop of the revisionist on 21.02.2003 at about 10 a.m. in which biscuits, toast, patties and pastry etc. being food items of bakery were found to be kept in an open place which were exposed to dust, smoke and flies and were displayed for sale. He made an inspection note and then filed a complaint. The Food Inspector Dalveer Singh was examined as P.W.1 under Section 246 Cr.P.C. There was no other witness produced in the trial. 6. The accused in his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. denied the prosecution case and stated that no raid was conducted in his premises and neither any food item was taken and sealed. He has a license to conduct the said business. The complaint has been filed on false allegations. He did not produce any defence witness. 7. The trial court perused the inspection report Exb. Ka-1, the departmental report Exb.Ka-2 and complaint as Exb. Ka-3. 8.
texts.arguments: 9. Learned counsel for the revisionist argued that the present case is not a case of adulteration. It is argued that the allegation against the revisionist is that the food stuff was kept in open in his shop and was thus exposed to dust, smoke and flies. It is argued that there is no credible evidence to show that any such occurrence has occurred. It is argued that NBW were issued against the revisionist after which he was arrested on 21.11.2023 and is in jail since then. Even previously the revisionist after his appeal being partly allowed vide judgement and order dated 23.1.2013 was granted bail on 6.2.2013 and as such had undergone 13 days in jail. As of now total period undergone by the revisionist is 2 months and 6 days out of total conviction of 3 months as awarded by the appellate court. It is argued that the revisionist has deposited the fine as imposed upon him. Learned counsel for the revisionist has placed the custody certificate which is annexure no.4 to the bail application. The present revision be thus allowed and revisionist be acquitted. 10. Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposed the arguments as aforesaid.
